newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed lower across the board as some of the confidence which propelled a three-month rally ebbed away for the time being at least.
The AEX index, which climbed from the low 500s in late July to just below the 600 mark last week closed 9.40 points lower at 581.75.
Dealers said there was an edgy feel to the market with the Dow dipping below 6,000 on Monday and talk in some quarters of a sharp downside correction looming.
A softer dollar and worries about a batch of U.S. economic indicators due this week also clouded sentiment.
One dealer said there had been a mood of apprehension ahead of today's U.S. employment costs and consumer confidence data.
"The figures actually looked okay and bonds rallied, but we just didn't have the strength to follow them," he added.
Another dealer said volume had not been very heavy but added that professionals had been selling off long positions.

Dealers said Wall Street guru Elaine Garzarelli's view that U.S. equities were set to fall 15-25 percent appeared to be taken seriously in some quarters, though most believed that the scope of a swing to lower levels would be more moderate.
"I would be surprised if the AEX went below 579," said one.
Several dealers said slightly lower price levels could provide a welcome stimulus.
"Our market has performed very well since July and was beginning to look a bit toppish. A correction would help clear the air and create room for people to step in again," said one.
Chemicals group DSM shed 5.10 at 161.50 after reporting lower than expected third quarter earnings and saying margins would remain under pressure in the fourth quarter.
Philips Electronics lost 2.10 at 59.20 in a reversal of gains posted last week following tough talk by new chairman Cor Boonstra prompted by a sharp drop in third quarter earnings.
One dealer dismissed this "Boonstra effect" which added 5.60 guilders to Philips' share price on Thursday and Friday as wishful thinking.
Royal Dutch Petroleum Co shed 4.40 guilders to 286.90 which dealers attributed to profit-taking after a strong run-up in the shares since early September.
